_comment: CARL built-in model catalogue. Downloaded and custom models are tracked separately in ~/.config/carl/models.json. Fields: hf (download source, pinned revision, sha256, bytes), tune (recommended server settings), why (the reason for each tuned value), ctx_zones (context per slot: <= good is fast (never below 96K, the floor), <= slow is usable, above very_slow is very slow; Auto-tune replaces these with measured values for this Mac), measured (reference measurements). Card fields: role (headline), good_for (tags: agent coding, hard code, chat & writing, uncensored), why_use, trade_offs, pick_instead (model + when), hardware, uncensored (what it means; abliterated models only), rank (quality order, 1 = best: published benchmarks and CARL's code test first, then quantization). draft (a separate MTP drafter, llama-server -md), speed (measured tok/s: prose, code, edit), fast (a small dense model auto fit's everyday goal takes with the MoE builds).

models.name: qwen3.6-35b-a3b
models.label: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B · Q4
models.summary: Default. Fast MoE: ~4x the decode and ~6x the prompt reading of the 27B, tiny context memory.
models.description: Stock Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (not abliterated), unsloth dynamic Q4_K_M with the MTP head. Only 3B parameters are active per token, so decode is bandwidth-cheap (42-45 tok/s new text, 117 re-emitting code on an M3 Pro) and its KV cache is tiny (5.6 KiB/token at q4_0): two 96K slots cost under 1 GiB of KV. Thinking is on/off only (no effort levels). Needs a 32 GB+ Mac; 24 GB Macs get the IQ3 build.

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: measured +16% cold prompt reading and ~2 GB less memory than q8_0, same decode speed and 8/8 needle recall at 66K. Never mix K and V types: mixed q8_0/q4_0 reads prompts ~5x slower on Metal.
why.temp: Qwen's thinking-mode recommendation from the model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0. Clients that send their own values (OpenCode's no-thinking variant) win per request.
why.spec: MTP (n=2) + n-gram: measured best on Q4_K_M (M3 Pro): 42-45 tok/s new text vs 33 without speculation, 117 tok/s re-emitting code. The n-gram drafter copies repeated text (edits, file rewrites) almost for free.
why.ctx: 96K per slot: cold reads stay fast (64K reads at 229 tok/s, 128K at 117 tok/s on the M3 Pro). 128K-160K work with 8/8 recall but every cold re-read takes 4x longer.
why.slots: 2 slots: the main OpenCode session and a coder subagent each keep their own cache; the follow-up after a subagent takes 0.6 s instead of a full re-read.

models.why_use: The fastest good model: only 3B parameters work per token, so it writes ~4x faster and reads prompts ~6x faster than the 27B, and its tiny context memory fits two 96K slots (main session + subagent) in under 1 GiB.
models.trade_offs: Weaker than the 27B on hard code (large refactors, subtle bugs, long reasoning); thinking is on/off only (no effort levels).

pick_instead.when: a task is too hard for it and you can wait (quality agent coding)

models.name: qwen3.8-27b
models.label: Qwen3.8 27B · Q4
models.summary: Stock dense 27B: slower (~11 tok/s) but stronger per token; effort levels for thinking.
models.description: Stock Qwen3.8-27B (not abliterated), unsloth dynamic Q4_K_M with the MTP head. Dense: every parameter is read for every token, so decode is ~11 tok/s and prompt reading ~85-90 tok/s. Same architecture and speed profile as the measured orcarouter build. Thinking supports effort levels (low/medium/xhigh, none = off). Its KV cache is 3x the 35B's (18 KiB/token at q4_0).

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: measured +16% cold prompt reading and ~2 GB less memory than q8_0, same decode speed and 8/8 needle recall at 66K. Never mix K and V types: mixed q8_0/q4_0 reads prompts ~5x slower on Metal.
why.temp: Qwen's thinking-mode recommendation from the model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0. Clients that send their own values (OpenCode's no-thinking variant) win per request.
why.spec: MTP n=1 + n-gram: measured best on the dense 27B (10.5-11 tok/s new text vs 7.4 without, 27 tok/s re-emitting). n>1 loses on Metal for dense models: the extra draft verify costs more than it saves.
why.ctx: 96K per slot, the floor CARL keeps (agents need that much context). On the 27B a cold read of a long session is slow (~56-65 tok/s at 66K: a full 96K window takes ~25 min), so windows above 96K are flagged as slow.
why.slots: 2 slots keep the main session cached while a subagent runs (1.9 s follow-up). Both generating at once time-share: no combined speed-up on dense models.

models.why_use: The strongest stock model in CARL: all 27B parameters work on every token, so it handles harder code and reasoning than the A3B, and thinking has effort levels (low / medium / xhigh). The choice for quality agent coding when you can accept the speed.
models.trade_offs: Slow: ~4x slower writing than the A3B and ~6x slower prompt reading (a cold read of a full 96K session takes many minutes); its context memory is 3x the A3B's.

models.label: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B · IQ3_XXS
models.summary: The 35B MoE in ~3-bit for 24 GB Macs. MTP + n-gram at n=1 (n=2 loses on IQ quants).
models.description: Stock Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, unsloth dynamic IQ3_XXS (~3-bit). Default on 24 GB Macs: 2 x 96K slots fit in ~15.3 GiB. IQ formats use lookup tables that unpack more slowly on Metal than K-quants; with only 3B active parameters decode is still fast (~45-50 tok/s on an M2 Max).

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: measured +16% cold prompt reading and ~2 GB less memory than q8_0, same decode speed and 8/8 needle recall at 66K. Never mix K and V types: mixed q8_0/q4_0 reads prompts ~5x slower on Metal.

why.spec: MTP + n-gram, n=1. Measured on an M2 Max 32 GB (2026-10-03, llama.cpp 0.5.0, 400-token runs, mean of 2, tok/s prose/code/re-emit): none 49/45/46, MTP n=1 47/44/46, MTP n=2 40/41/49, n-gram 47/42/117, MTP+n-gram n=1 49/50/93, MTP+n-gram n=2 42/43/83. MTP alone adds nothing on IQ3 (the IQ kernels make the draft verify expensive) and n=2 costs ~15%; with n-gram at n=1 it is the best overall (n-gram alone wins only on re-emitting).
why.ctx: 96K per slot: the MoE KV cache is tiny, so long windows cost little memory; cold reads slow down past 128K.
why.slots: 2 slots fit even on 24 GB Macs: main session + subagent.

models.name: qwen3.8-9b
models.label: Qwen3.8 9B Distill · Q4_K_M
models.summary: A small distilled Qwen (5.8 GB): room for 3-4 subagent slots on larger Macs. On 16 GB Macs the Gemma 4 E4B and 12B are better.
models.description: empero-ai's Qwen3.8-9B-Distill: a community full-parameter distillation of Qwen3.8 (2.4T-A95B) into the Qwen3.5-9B hybrid architecture (Apache-2.0); not an official Qwen release (Qwen publishes no 9B in the 3.8 line). The publisher's Q4_K_M, with the MTP head. It thinks by default; thinking is on / off only (no effort levels). The hybrid layers decode slowly on Metal: ~25 tok/s on an M2 Max (llama-bench agrees: CARL's flags cost nothing), about half the 35B-A3B MoE, which reads only 3B parameters per token. Its small weights leave room for 2 x 96K on a 16 GB Mac, where no other catalogue model fits, or for 3-4 slots on larger Macs.

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: measured +16% cold prompt reading and ~2 GB less memory than q8_0 on the 35B, the same decode speed and 8/8 needle recall at 66K. Never mix K and V types: mixed q8_0/q4_0 reads prompts ~5x slower on Metal.

why.spec: MTP + n-gram, n=1. Auto-tune on an M2 Max 32 GB (2026-10-03, llama.cpp 0.5.0, tok/s prose/code/re-emit): none 24.8/24.1/24.3, n-gram n=2 23.7/24.3/112.5, MTP n=1 24.9/24.1/27.7, MTP+n-gram n=1 25.8/25.8/103.7 (the best score). New text barely speeds up; re-emitting code does ~4x.

why.slots: auto: 2 slots when two windows fit (a 16 GB Mac fits 2 x 96K). For more subagents at once set 3-4 where they fit (Server panel): measured on an M2 Max (llama-batched-bench, 1K-token prompts) 25 / 29 / 41 tok/s in total with 1 / 2 / 4 requests at once, so 4 at once is 1.6x the throughput but ~10 tok/s each. 8 slots would fit, but each request falls to ~6 tok/s (45 in total): CARL stops at 4.

measured.decode: ~25 tok/s new text, ~104 re-emitting (MTP+n-gram n=1); 29 / 41 tok/s in total with 2 / 4 requests at once

models.name: gemma-4-e4b
models.label: Gemma 4 E4B · Q4_0 QAT
models.summary: Google's small Gemma 4 (4.6 GB): fast on any Mac, Google's QAT Q4_0; auto fit's everyday pick on 16 GB Macs; weaker than the 12B and up on hard code.
models.description: Stock Gemma 4 E4B instruction-tuned (Apache-2.0), Google's quantization-aware-trained (QAT) weights quantized to Q4_0 by ggml-org (token embedding at Q8_0): Google says QAT keeps quality close to bfloat16, and Q4_0 is the fastest 4-bit format on Metal. 42 layers, 18 of which reuse earlier layers' KV; 4 full-attention layers (4.5 KiB/token at q4_0) and 20 sliding-window layers (window 512; 11.2 KiB/token at q4_0 when kept at full length with --swa-full, which a restored prompt state needs). 2 x 96K with the full cache needs ~8.2 GiB: it fits a 16 GB Mac. Trained context 128K. Thinking is on / off only (no effort levels); llama-server turns it on by default, reasoning_effort none turns it off. Its per-layer embeddings (2.1 GiB of the file) stay in CPU memory, so it uses less GPU memory than the estimate. Text and images in the model; CARL starts it text-only (--no-mmproj).

why.kv: q4_0 K and V like every catalogue model (measured on the Qwen builds: faster cold reads, less memory, same recall). Checked on this M2 Max with llama.cpp 0.5.0: flash attention works with q4_0 K/V at Gemma's 512-wide global heads, and the KV sizes llama.cpp allocates match CARL's estimate (2 x 64K: 576 MiB full-attention + 1440 MiB sliding-window with --swa-full, 16.9 MiB window-only). Never mix K and V types.
why.temp: Google's model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64 for all uses (the GGUF's general.sampling says the same); min_p not given, 0.
why.spec: MTP + n-gram, 2 draft tokens. Measured 2026-10-04 (llama.cpp 0.5.0 on the M2 Max, 0.4.1 on the M3 Pro; temperature 0, thinking off; 700 tokens of new code, ~600 of prose, a 110-line file re-emitted with one rename; tok/s, then Auto-tune's weighted score): M2 Max, Auto-tune: none 48.9 / 50.4 / 48.3 (score 49.4); n-gram n=2 49.8 / 48.7 / 275.9 (69.5); MTP n=2 54.2 / 56.7 / 72.2 (58.4); MTP + n-gram n=2 56.8 / 59.1 / 240.8 (77.0, the best). MTP speeds new text (66-80% of its drafts accepted); n-gram speeds re-emitted code (it drafts nothing on new text). The drafter is ggml-org mtp-gemma-4-E4B-it-Q4_0.gguf (60 MB, QAT): llama-server loads it with -md and it shares the target's KV cache, so only its weights add memory. Without the drafter downloaded, a start uses n-gram.
why.ctx: 96K per slot, the floor CARL keeps; the trained length is 128K, the most it can take. llama-bench on an M2 Max (q4_0 KV, window cache): 894 tok/s at 512, 581 tok/s at 8K, so long cold reads are quick.
why.slots: auto: 2 x 96K with the full sliding-window cache (~8.2 GiB) fits every Mac from 16 GB up; on larger Macs 3-4 slots fit for subagents.

models.role: Small and fast: Google's Gemma 4 for any Mac
models.why_use: About twice the decode speed of the Qwen3.8 9B on the same Mac (llama-bench, M2 Max: 46 vs 24 tok/s, no speculation) at a smaller size (4.6 GB): 2 × 96K slots fit a 16 GB Mac, and larger Macs have room for 3-4 slots. Google's QAT weights keep Q4_0 close to full precision.
models.trade_offs: Only 4.5B effective parameters: well below the 26B-A4B and the Qwen models on code and agent tasks (Google: LiveCodeBench 52% vs 77% for the 26B-A4B, Tau2 42% vs 68%). Trained context 128K, not 256K. Not tested at length for agent coding.

pick_instead.when: you want better code and can wait: it thinks much longer (Auto fit's hard-code choice on 16 GB)
it fits (24 GB and up): much better at agent coding
a 32 GB+ Mac and you want Gemma 4 for real coding work

models.hardware: 16 GB Macs and up (2 × 96K with the full cache ~8.2 GiB); larger Macs for 3-4 slots

models.name: gemma-4-12b
models.label: Gemma 4 12B · Q4_0 QAT
models.summary: Google's dense Gemma 4 12B (7.2 GB): strong code for its size; 2 × 96K fits a 16 GB Mac with the window cache.
models.description: Stock Gemma 4 12B instruction-tuned (Apache-2.0), Google's quantization-aware-trained (QAT) weights quantized to Q4_0 by ggml-org; Q4_0 is the fastest 4-bit format on Metal. 48 layers, none sharing KV: 8 full-attention (1 KV head x 512: 4.5 KiB/token at q4_0) and 40 sliding-window (window 1024, 8 KV heads x 256: 90 KiB/token at q4_0 when kept at full length with --swa-full, which a restored prompt state needs). With its MTP drafter, 2 x 96K needs ~9.1 GiB with the window-only cache (fits a 16 GB Mac) and ~25.7 GiB with the full cache. Trained context 256K. Thinking is on / off only; llama-server turns it on by default. Text and images in the model; CARL starts it text-only (--no-mmproj).

why.kv: q4_0 K and V like every catalogue model: the sliding-window layers cost 90 KiB/token at full length even at q4_0, so q8_0 would double the largest cost. Never mix K and V types.
why.temp: Google's model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64 for all uses; min_p not given, 0.
why.spec: MTP + n-gram, 2 draft tokens. Measured 2026-10-04 (llama.cpp 0.5.0 on the M2 Max, 0.4.1 on the M3 Pro; temperature 0, thinking off; 700 tokens of new code, ~600 of prose, a 110-line file re-emitted with one rename; tok/s, then Auto-tune's weighted score): M2 Max 32 GB, prose / code / re-emit: none 26.7 / 27.2 / 25.6 (score 26.7); n-gram n=2 26.7 / 27.2 / 132.7 (37.1); MTP n=2 29.9 / 36.8 / 36.1 (33.7); MTP n=3-4 lose on prose (28.1, 26.3); MTP + n-gram n=2 28.2 / 34.3 / 129.4 (41.4, the best); n=3 40.8. The drafter is ggml-org mtp-gemma-4-12B-it-Q4_0.gguf (0.25 GB, QAT): llama-server loads it with -md and it shares the target's KV cache. Without the drafter downloaded, a start uses n-gram.
why.ctx: 96K per slot, the floor CARL keeps; the trained length is 256K. With the window-only cache long windows cost little (4.5 KiB/token); with the full cache the largest 2-slot window is 8K on a 16 GB Mac, 40K on 24 GB, 84K on 32 GB and 100K on 36 GB.
why.slots: auto: 2 x 96K with the window-only cache (~9.1 GiB with the drafter) fits every Mac from 16 GB up (cache.swa auto picks the window when the full cache does not fit: a second slot wins over restorable states); the full cache (~25.7 GiB at 2 x 96K) needs a 36 GB Mac.

models.role: Dense Gemma 4 12B: strong coding for its size, 16 GB+ Macs
models.why_use: Much stronger than the E4B on Google's benchmarks and close to the 26B-A4B (LiveCodeBench v6 72.0% vs 52.0% for the E4B and 77.1% for the 26B-A4B; Codeforces ELO 1659 vs 940 and 1718; GPQA Diamond 78.8%, Tau2 69.0%, MMLU Pro 77.2%) at 7.2 GB: 2 × 96K with the window cache fits a 16 GB Mac. Google's QAT weights keep Q4_0 close to full precision.
models.trade_offs: Not measured in CARL yet (speed, recall, agent coding). Dense, so each generated token reads all 7.2 GB: slower than the MoE models. Its full-length sliding-window cache is large (90 KiB/token), so on most Macs it runs with the window cache, and saved prompt states restore only with the full cache (25.7 GiB at 2 × 96K). Thinking is on/off only.

pick_instead.when: it fits (24 GB and up): faster, and better at agent coding
a 36 GB Mac: the faster MoE
you want the fastest small model

models.hardware: 16 GB Macs and up (2 × 96K with the window cache, 9.1 GiB); the full cache needs a 32 GB Mac or more for long windows

models.name: gemma-4-26b-a4b
models.label: Gemma 4 26B-A4B · Q4_0 QAT
models.summary: Google's Gemma 4 MoE (14.6 GB): 3.8B active per token; 2 × 96K with the full cache fits a 36 GB Mac.
models.description: Stock Gemma 4 26B-A4B instruction-tuned (Apache-2.0): 128 experts, 8 active + 1 shared, 3.8B parameters per token. Google's QAT weights quantized to Q4_0 by ggml-org (token embedding Q8_0); Q4_0 is the fastest 4-bit format on Metal. 30 layers: 5 full-attention (2 KV heads x 512: 5.6 KiB/token at q4_0) and 25 sliding-window (window 1024, 8 KV heads x 256: 56 KiB/token at q4_0 at full length). With --swa-full (needed to restore a saved prompt state) 2 x 96K needs ~26.2 GiB: it fits a 36 GB Mac (28.1 GiB GPU limit), not a 32 GB one, where CARL keeps 2 slots and the window-only cache (~15.8 GiB; saved states don't restore). Trained context 256K. Thinking is on / off only; llama-server turns it on by default. Text and images in the model; CARL starts it text-only.

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: at q8_0 the sliding-window layers alone cost 106 KiB/token at full length, and 2 x 96K with --swa-full no longer fits a 36 GB Mac (36.5 GiB). Never mix K and V types.
why.temp: Google's model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64 for all uses; min_p not given, 0.

The drafter is ggml-org mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q4_0.gguf (0.25 GB, QAT): llama-server loads it with -md and it shares the target's KV cache. Without the drafter downloaded, a start uses n-gram.

why.slots: auto: 2 x 96K with the full cache on a 36 GB Mac (26.2 GiB of 28.1); on a 32 GB Mac (25.0 GiB limit) 2 slots fit only with the window cache (cache.swa auto picks it: a second slot wins over restorable states), or 1 x 96K with the full cache (20.4 GiB).

models.role: Gemma 4 MoE: fast everyday coding on 36 GB Macs
models.why_use: Google's MoE alternative to the Qwen 35B-A3B: 3.8B parameters per token keep decode fast, the QAT Q4_0 weights are 8 GB smaller than the Qwen build (14.6 vs 22.7 GB), and on a 36 GB Mac two 96K slots fit with the full sliding-window cache, so saved prompt states restore. Strong for its size on Google's benchmarks (LiveCodeBench 77%, GPQA 82%).
models.trade_offs: Not measured in CARL yet (speed, recall, agent coding). Its full-length sliding-window cache is 10x the Qwen 35B-A3B's KV (62 vs 5.6 KiB/token), so above 2 × 108K or on a 32 GB Mac it runs with the window cache (saved prompt states don't restore). Thinking is on/off only.

a task is too hard for it and you can wait

models.name: gemma-4-31b
models.label: Gemma 4 31B · Q4_0 QAT
models.summary: Google's dense Gemma 4 31B (18 GB): the strongest Gemma; slow, and only the window cache fits.
models.description: Stock Gemma 4 31B instruction-tuned (Apache-2.0), Google's QAT weights quantized to Q4_0 by ggml-org (token embedding Q8_0). Dense: all 31B parameters are read for every token (~18 GB per token), so decode is bandwidth-bound and slow. 60 layers: 10 full-attention (4 KV heads x 512: 22.5 KiB/token at q4_0) and 50 sliding-window (window 1024, 16 KV heads x 256: 225 KiB/token at q4_0 at full length). The full-length cache (--swa-full) is out of reach below ~96 GB of RAM (2 x 96K: 64 GiB), so CARL runs it with the window-only cache: 2 x 96K needs ~22.6 GiB (36 GB and 32 GB Macs), but saved prompt states don't restore. Trained context 256K. Thinking is on / off only; llama-server turns it on by default. Text and images in the model; CARL starts it text-only.

why.kv: q4_0 K and V: with the window-only cache 2 x 96K needs 22.6 GiB at q4_0 and 27.0 GiB at q8_0 (only just under a 36 GB Mac's 28.1). Never mix K and V types.
why.temp: Google's model card: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64 for all uses; min_p not given, 0.
why.spec: MTP + n-gram, 2 guesses. Measured 2026-10-04 on the M3 Pro 36 GB (llama.cpp 0.4.1; temperature 0, thinking off; ~600 tokens of prose, 700 of new code, a 110-line file re-emitted with one rename), prose / code / re-emit tok/s and Auto-tune's score: none 7.0 / 7.0 / 6.7 (6.9); n-gram n=2 7.1 / 7.0 / 43.8 (10.2); MTP n=1 8.9 / 9.5 / 9.4 (9.2), n=2 9.2 / 10.6 / 11.2 (10.1), n=4 5.6 / 7.4 / 8.7 (6.8); MTP + n-gram n=1 8.9 / 9.5 / 45.8 (12.7), n=2 8.7 / 10.0 / 46.2 (12.8), n=3 (11.9). n=2 is the best: three more runs of n=1 and n=2 gave the same numbers each time (this model is deterministic at temperature 0 here), so its 0.8% lead is real; Auto-tune's 3% margin (it guards against run-to-run noise) would keep n=1 on this Mac. The drafter is ggml-org mtp-gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_0.gguf (0.28 GB, QAT): llama-server loads it with -md and it shares the target's context memory. Without the drafter downloaded, a start uses n-gram.
why.ctx: 96K per slot, the floor CARL keeps. With the window-only cache the largest window is ~220K per slot on a 36 GB Mac (2 slots), ~148K on a 32 GB Mac; with --swa-full it would be 20K (2 slots) / 40K (1 slot) on a 36 GB Mac.
why.slots: auto: 2 x 96K with the window-only cache (cache.swa auto picks it: the full cache does not fit) on 36 and 32 GB Macs; 1 slot on a 32 GB Mac with the VM up (22 GiB allowed).

models.role: Gemma 4 dense 31B: hard code when you can wait
models.why_use: The strongest Gemma 4 and the largest stock dense model that fits a 32-36 GB Mac: Google reports LiveCodeBench 80%, Codeforces 2150, Tau2 77% (26B-A4B: 77% / 1718 / 68%), and the QAT Q4_0 weights keep it close to full precision.
models.trade_offs: Slow: dense, ~18 GB read per generated token (MTP speculation with its drafter is not measured yet; expect below the Qwen 27B's ~11 tok/s on an M3 Pro). Runs only with the window cache sliding-window cache on these Macs, so saved prompt states don't restore after a restart or eviction. Not measured in CARL yet.

pick_instead.when: hard code with CARL's measured setup (MTP speculation, effort levels, restorable prompt states)

models.hardware: 36 GB Macs (2 × 96K, window cache: 22.6 GiB); also fits 32 GB Macs (2 × 96K; 1 slot with the VM up)
